intended_object: The finite cyclic group ℤ/p^nℤ (= ℤ_p/p^nℤ_p) with the discrete topology, seen as a profinite additive group (lifted to universe u). This is the finite-exponent factor of the primewise p-adic quotient model. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the way `padicQuotientFactor` uses it.
explanation:
The body takes `ZMod (p ^ n)` with Mathlib's discrete topology and lifts it to universe `u` with `ULift`, which carries the induced topology. It then shows the lift is compact and totally disconnected by transporting both properties along `Homeomorph.ulift`, and bundles it with `ProfiniteAddGrp.of`. The result is exactly ℤ/p^nℤ as a finite discrete, and hence profinite, additive group. The degenerate case n = 0 gives the trivial group `ZMod 1`, which is the right quotient of ℤ_p by the unit ideal; the file states this case explicitly elsewhere.

The definition names a specific group. Restricting to prime powers p^n, rather than allowing any modulus m, is part of its role as the finite branch of the p-adic factor family. That is not an unnecessary narrowing. The universe lift is only a device to fit the chosen universe, and it does not change the mathematical object.

Mathlib has no bundled declaration for "ZMod (p^n) as a ProfiniteAddGrp"; it only has the general constructor `ProfiniteAddGrp.of`, which this definition uses. So the definition is faithful.
